Derailment mechanisms often involve lateral instability, vehicle overturning, and flange climb, posing safety risks and operational interruptions
The sources do not provide a definitive answer to specific derailment safety measures or solutions
The sources indicate that track geometry irregularities significantly impact railway safety and derailment risk

The derailment coefficient, which considers lateral and vertical forces generated by a wheel, is a key parameter for evaluating derailment risk (Predictive Models for Railway Track Geometry Degradation)

Track geometry defects, such as alignment, longitudinal level, twist, and gauge, can lead to large lateral wheel and axle forces, increasing derailment risk (Railway track geometry inspection optimization)
(2014) found that track geometry failure was the second leading cause of freight railroad derailments in the USA in 2009
Tensor analysis offers a new way to analyze track geometry and ballast conditions to improve safety and system performance (Improve railway safety with new way to analyze track conditions)
